lessons.culture: In Beirut many taxi meters are off or broken, so the price is agreed before you get in, and a little haggling is normal. Fares are said in thousands of lira, and drivers often drop the word ألف and just say the number (تلاتمية); some quote dollars instead.

lessons.culture: Beirut has few marked bus stops, so buses and shared vans are usually flagged down along the road, and the driver or his helper shouts the destination out loud. Vans and shared taxis charge a set price per seat, paid in cash, and you ask to get off by calling out "نزّلني هون".

exercises.tip: "نزّلني" means let me off; add the place after "عَ".

challenge.title: Getting Around Beirut
challenge.instructions: Write and act out a conversation of at least 10 lines about getting to a meeting place across town. It must include calling or boarding a taxi or van, asking the fare, asking for directions to a specific place, naming at least two places in town, and thanking the driver or the person who helped you. Use at least 8 target phrases from Unit 5 and include both a masculine-address and a feminine-address form.
required_elements: A request to a driver using بدّي روح عَ or a similar phrase.
A question about the fare using قدّيش.
At least one turn instruction using لِفّ or دغري.
At least two named places, for example السوق, الجامع, البنك, or المحطّة.
A thank-you exchange using شكراً كتير or يعطيك العافية.
One masculine-address form and one feminine-address form.

dialogue.speaker: ليال
dialogue.arabic: لو سمحت، بدّي روح عَ السوق.
dialogue.english: Please, I want to go to the market.

dialogue.speaker: شوفير
dialogue.english: Sure, get in.

dialogue.speaker: ليال
dialogue.english: How much do you want for the ride?

dialogue.speaker: شوفير
dialogue.english: Four hundred thousand.

dialogue.speaker: ليال
dialogue.arabic: تمام. وين أقرب بنك من السوق؟
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam. ween a2rab bank min es-sooq?
dialogue.english: Okay. Where's the nearest bank from the market?

dialogue.speaker: شوفير
dialogue.arabic: قريب، بعد الجامع عَ اليمين وبتلاقيه.
dialogue.english: Near, after the mosque on the right and you'll find it.

dialogue.speaker: ليال
dialogue.arabic: منيح. دغري لَحد السوق، وبعدين وقّف لو سمحت.
dialogue.transliteration: mneeh. dughri la7add es-sooq, w-ba3deen wa22ef law samaht.
dialogue.english: Good. Straight to the market, then stop please.

dialogue.speaker: شوفير
dialogue.english: Here you go, we arrived.

dialogue.speaker: ليال
dialogue.english: How much is the bill?

dialogue.speaker: شوفير
dialogue.english: Just four hundred thousand.

dialogue.speaker: ليال
dialogue.english: Here, and keep the change. Thanks a lot.

dialogue.speaker: شوفير
dialogue.english: Thank you, God be with you.

transliteration_key.2: ء / ق (في اللهجة اللبنانية تُنطق همزة)
